purpose: We read papers on causal inference together: how effects are identified, how they are estimated, and where the assumptions break. Sessions are expository and discussion-driven; presenters do not need to be working on the topic.

tracks.name: Theory
tracks.description: Identification arguments, proofs and the assumptions behind them.

tracks.name: Practice
tracks.description: Estimators in use: code walkthroughs, replications and applied papers.

scope.intro: Topics are chosen by members, so this is a map rather than a fixed syllabus. Anything connected to causal reasoning can be proposed.

steps: The presenter sets up the problem: which causal question is being asked, and what data would answer it.
We work through the identifying assumptions and the key argument or estimator, slowing down at the steps that matter.
The last 20 minutes are open discussion: limitations, links to earlier sessions, and what to read next.
format.note: Practice sessions can add a code walkthrough, a replication or a small simulation. A session can cover a single theorem or section rather than a whole paper.

participation.intro: Sessions are open to anyone, including people outside the group and prospective students. Come to listen and ask questions, or volunteer to present something you want to understand better.
